dedupe_keys.name: cabinet office nankai trough megaquake 2025 tsunami fault model data onshore tsunami inundation depth grids by case with and without levee failure

description: In 2025 the Cabinet Office of Japan published the calculation results behind its revised Nankai Trough megaquake model report, including item (11), onshore tsunami inundation depth data. Contents: gridded maximum inundation depths on land for each tsunami fault case of the revised model, provided in two variants: files marked levee failure (堤防破堤), in which coastal levees are assumed to fail, and files in which levees function regardless of shaking, together with a description of the calculation results and the terms of use; a parallel dataset exists for the Tokyo inland (Shuto chokka) earthquake model. Producer: the Cabinet Office's review committee on the Nankai Trough megaquake model and damage estimation methods (from 2025). Coverage: the Pacific coast of Japan from Kanto to Kyushu that is exposed to Nankai Trough tsunamis. Format and access: ZIP archives of grid data per case, downloadable from the G-Spatial Information Center, with PDF documentation; updated in March 2026. Free under the Cabinet Office's own terms of use. Caveats: files are large and use Japanese grid conventions described in the PDF; depths are scenario results for maximum-class events, not probabilistic hazard. Simulation uses: tsunami exposure of ports, roads, rail, power and water facilities and buildings, levee-failure sensitivity analysis, and inputs to national damage estimation and evacuation models. Related records: the Nankai Trough lifeline countermeasures material (data-japan-nankai-trough-lifeline-countermeasures-2023) and the MLIT Social Infrastructure Information Platform (data-japan-mlit-social-infrastructure-information-platform).
